unit_name: French 1st Infantry Division (1st Free French Division)
current_activity: After Toulon the division goes up the Rhone valley and reaches Lyon
notes: Event date: 3 September 1944 (Wikipedia; CMH Riviera to the Rhine, p. 181). Event definition: Landed in Provence on 15 August, the division fights at Toulon, sends reconnaissance squadrons to Montpellier and goes up the Rhone, reaching Lyon on 3 September. Event support: three source families (Wikipedia, the US Army official history (CMH) and de Lattre's History of the French First Army). Wikipedia, 1st Free French Division, section 1944: "With First Army, the division disembarked in Provence on 15 August 1944 and participated in the Battle of Toulon, then went up the Rhône"; "Lyon was reached on 3 September"; CMH Riviera to the Rhine ch. 10 p. 181: "In the west, French units of the 1st Infantry Division, after overcoming scattered German roadblocks and their own logistical problems, had entered Lyon earlier, on the 3d, and also found the Germans long gone"; de Lattre, The History of the French First Army (1952) p. 128: "the division penetrated Lyons on the 3rd September at eight in the morning". Location: Lyon, Palais de la Foire (east bank of the Rhône), Rhône with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the point is an existing point in Lyon; the sources give only the city. Location support: Wikipedia and the CMH history both name Lyon and 3 September for the division: two source families for a city-level place (precision 10 km), so 0.7. French follow-up: confidence raised from 0.5 to 0.7 after the CMH history (p. 181) was read as a second source family. Commander: General Diego Brosset commands the division until his death on 20 November 1944 (Wikipedia). French follow-up (de Lattre): de Lattre (p. 128) has the 1st DFL (Brosset) enter Lyon at 08.00 on 3 September, the 36th US Division halting to let it in; a third source family that confirms the day; the place is still the city (precision 10 km), so confidence stays 0.7. Activity: in_line, span point, stated; in the activity rollout, Canada and France (October 2026), the old value of activity_status is blank, the new value is in_line (point, stated); reason: the cited source has the division advancing against the enemy, which is line service.

notes: Event date: 23 January 1945 (Wikipedia; CMH Riviera to the Rhine, p. 536). Event definition: In the II Corps offensive on the northern face of the Colmar Pocket, the division attacks east toward the Rhine on 23 January, covering the northern flank of the US 3d Division. Event support: two source families (Wikipedia and the US Army official history (CMH)). Wikipedia, Colmar Pocket, section Push to the Rhine in the north: "General Garbay's French 1st Infantry Marching Division attacked to the east on 23 January with the Rhine River as their objective"; CMH Riviera to the Rhine ch. 29 p. 536: "On its left, the French 1st Infantry Division, with some of Leclerc's armor attached, would push east, covering the northern flank of the American unit". Location: Sélestat, Bas-Rhin with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the point stands for the start line south of Selestat; precision 10 km. Location support: the place is a representative point (inferred value): the sources give only the direction of attack; the offensive started from the area south of Selestat (CMH, p. 535); precision 10 km. Commander: General Pierre Garbay commands the division from 20 November 1944 (Wikipedia).
